Maria (Product): Quick sync: leadership wants us to pick a single path for tenant isolation + prefetch for Q3 pilot. This is customer-driven (healthcare & fintech) — needs SLA, KMS support, and a clear rollback policy.
Ravi (Eng-runtime): what are the non-negotiable SLAs? latency, token cost, and isolation boundaries?
Maria (Product): non-negotiables: 1) p99 latency target for small prompts <= 250ms under canary loads, 2) strict tenant KV separation (no cross-tenant cache reuse), 3) deterministic cost accounting per-request. Nice-to-have: predictive prefetch tuning that adjusts by tenant.
Lena (Eng-infra): for strict isolation we need per-tenant pools or strong namespacing on the cache layer. Per-tenant pools increases infra cost ~20% based on initial estimates. Need capacity numbers for pilots.
Olivia (Security): KMS integration must support both service-managed keys and customer-provided keys (BYOK). Audit trail must show key_id, tenant_id, action. Also need threat model signoff.
Priya (ProdOps): runbook ask: who responds when isolation pool drains? define escalation: infra -> runtime -> product. Also what user-visible behavior? 429 vs degraded output?
Ravi (Eng-runtime): runtime tasks: - add tenant affinity routing - implement strict namespace for KV cache - prefetch controller that can be enabled per-tenant. We'll need an infra API to request a dedicated pool: POST /tenant_pools {tenant_id, region, size}.
Lena (Eng-infra): API spec looks fine. We will prototype with 5 pilot tenants. Question: how big is a "slot"? define slot in terms of GPU mem & concurrency.
Maria (Product): pilot tenants: NimbusHealth (HIPAA), AtlasBank (PCI), and two smaller startups. Expected peak per-tenant qps during pilot: 25 req/s, avg tokens 120. Start with pool size 3 per tenant in region.
Nate (SRE): monitoring: we need tenant-level SLO dashboards, alerts for cache isolation violations (this should be a high-severity finding), and pool_exhausted alerts. Suggest pool_exhausted > 2/min -> SEV3, sustained > 30/min -> SEV2.
Olivia (Security): also require signed audit entries for pool allocation and KMS operations. Encryption in transit+at-rest for pool metadata.
Priya (ProdOps): user-visible decision: on pool exhaustion we should 1) queue briefly up to 500ms, 2) if still blocked return 429 with a structured body explaining "isolation_pool_exhausted" and hint to retry-after. This is better than silent fallback for regulated customers.
Ravi (Eng-runtime): we can implement short queue + backpressure. For non-regulated customers we can optionally fallback to shared-prequant model with a quality guard. Make this tenant-configurable.
Lena (Eng-infra): infra constraints: per-tenant pools require scheduler changes. Need an autoscaler hook to spin up cold pools and a leak detector to free abandoned pools. ETA: scheduler changes in 2 weeks, leak detector + RBAC in 3 weeks.
Maria (Product): proposed launch gates: (1) security signoff on KMS + audit, (2) infra API and scheduler changes in staging, (3) runtime tenant-affinity & prefetch controller + unit tests, (4) ProdOps runbook + paging roster, (5) pilot onboarding with acceptance test results.
Nate (SRE): acceptance tests: simulate pool exhaustion, failover to shared model (where allowed), ensure p99 < 350ms and error-rate < 0.7%. Also run isolation fuzz tests to detect KV bleed.
Olivia (Security): threat modeling: I'll schedule a 1h review Wed afternoon. Need initial design doc from Ravi by Tue EOD.
Ravi (Eng-runtime): will drop the design doc today: routing, prefetch controller algorithm (LRU+predictive warm), and telemetry events: pool_allocated, pool_released, isolation_violation (shouldn't happen). Example event JSON I'll emit in PR.
Priya (ProdOps): runbook sketch: 1) monitor pool_exhausted alert -> 2) run quick recovery (increase pool via infra API) -> 3) if recovery fails, page infra oncall -> 4) notify tenant success team. I'll circulate with oncall roster.
Lena (Eng-infra): RBAC: pool allocation must be restricted to internal service accounts; tenant owners can request but must be approved. We'll add a request queue and approval flow.
Maria (Product): timeline ask: leadership wants a controlled pilot in 4 weeks. Can we hit that? Ravi/Lena give a short callout.
Ravi (Eng-runtime): optimistic: runtime work in 2 weeks for tenant-affinity + prefetch toggles. Needs infra scheduler in place week 2. So pilot in 4 weeks looks feasible if infra keeps schedule.
Lena (Eng-infra): agreed but risk: autoscaler and leak detector are the biggest blockers. If those slip, pilot goes to 6 weeks. I'll provide a risk note by Mon.
Olivia (Security): will block pilot if audit or BYOK path incomplete for regulated tenants. Non-regulated tenants can go earlier under feature flag.
Maria (Product): final assignment: - @Lena: scheduler API + RBAC prototype by Mon - @Ravi: design doc + telemetry schema by Tue - @Olivia: threat model slot Wed + audit checklist by Thu - @Priya: runbook draft by Wed - @Nate: monitoring & chaos plan by Thu.
deploy-bot: deploy window requested: 2026-07-02 03:00-06:00 UTC for scheduler updates.
Nate (SRE): add me to that window. We'll run pool exhaustion chaos after deploy.
Lena (Eng-infra): ack. I'll publish initial capacity cost estimate by Tue.
Maria (Product): thanks team. We'll reconvene Fri for go/no-go micro-check. Please file action items in the initiative epic and ping me if anything blocks.
